trapezius.name: Trapezius
trapezius.function: Lifts, squeezes and steadies the shoulder blades and supports the head.
trapezius.running: Holds the shoulders down and back so the arms can swing freely; tension here shrugs the shoulders up.
trapezius.injury: Neck and upper-back tension from a forward head or hunched, high shoulders.

deltoid.name: Deltoid
deltoid.function: Raises the arm forwards, sideways and backwards.
deltoid.running: Drives the forward-and-back arm swing that balances the legs.
deltoid.injury: Shoulder strain or impingement from overuse.

pectoralis_major.name: Pectoralis major
pectoralis_major.function: Pulls the arm in front of the body and down.
pectoralis_major.running: Controls the forward part of the arm swing; it should not pull the arms across the body.
pectoralis_major.injury: Tight chest muscles round the shoulders forward and spoil running posture.

biceps.name: Biceps brachii
biceps.function: Bends the elbow and turns the palm up.
biceps.running: Holds the elbow at roughly 90 degrees through the arm swing.
biceps.injury: Biceps tendinopathy at the shoulder or the elbow.

triceps.name: Triceps brachii
triceps.function: Straightens the elbow and pulls the arm back.
triceps.running: Powers the backward part of the arm swing.

forearm.name: Forearm flexors and extensors
forearm.function: Control the wrist and fingers and produce grip.
forearm.running: Should stay relaxed: loose hands save energy.
forearm.injury: Tennis / golfer's elbow from repetitive gripping.

hand.name: Hand muscles
hand.running: A loose, cupped hand avoids tension travelling up the arm.

latissimus_dorsi.name: Latissimus dorsi
latissimus_dorsi.function: Pulls the arm down and back and helps stabilise the spine.
latissimus_dorsi.running: Links each arm swing with the opposite hip through the back fascia.
latissimus_dorsi.injury: Tight lats limit overhead reach and can pull the shoulders forward.

erector_spinae.name: Erector spinae
erector_spinae.function: Straightens the spine and holds it upright.
erector_spinae.running: Controls the forward lean of the trunk on every stride.
erector_spinae.injury: Low-back pain from fatigue or an over-arched back.

rectus_abdominis.name: Rectus abdominis
rectus_abdominis.function: Bends the trunk forward and braces the core.
rectus_abdominis.running: Stops the pelvis tipping forward, which protects the lower back.
rectus_abdominis.injury: Abdominal strain; a weak core lets the lower back arch.

external_oblique.name: External oblique
external_oblique.running: Controls trunk rotation against the arm swing.

serratus_anterior.name: Serratus anterior
serratus_anterior.function: Holds the shoulder blade flat against the ribs and rotates it upward.
serratus_anterior.running: Keeps the shoulder blades stable while the arms swing.

scm.name: Sternocleidomastoid
scm.region: Front and side of the neck
scm.function: Turns the head and bends the neck forward.
scm.running: Should stay quiet; a forward-poking head overloads it.
scm.injury: Neck strain and tension headaches with a forward head posture.

jaw.name: Masseter and temporalis
jaw.running: Clenching the jaw while running wastes energy and tightens the neck.

gluteus_maximus.name: Gluteus maximus
gluteus_maximus.function: Extends the hip (moves the thigh back).
gluteus_maximus.running: The main push-off muscle of the stride.
gluteus_maximus.injury: Weak glutes lead to knee collapse, IT-band and low-back problems.

gluteus_medius.name: Gluteus medius
gluteus_medius.function: Moves the thigh out to the side and keeps the pelvis level.
gluteus_medius.running: Stops the opposite hip dropping while standing on one leg.
gluteus_medius.injury: Weakness causes hip drop, IT-band syndrome and runner's knee.

hip_flexors.name: Hip flexors (iliopsoas)
hip_flexors.running: Swing the leg through for the next step.
hip_flexors.injury: Tight hip flexors tilt the pelvis forward and load the lower back; hip-flexor strain.
